sources.t: San Francisco Ethics Commission: Form 700 Schedule C - income, loans and business positions (DataSF)
San Francisco Controller: Vendor Payments (Vouchers), totals by payee, department and fiscal year (DataSF)
San Francisco Ethics Commission: Form 3209b - notifications of recusal (DataSF)

tables.how: Every income source on a Form 700 Schedule C since 2019 is matched by name to the payees of the filer’s own department. A tie is kept when the department paid the source $25,000 or more in the fiscal years around the report. Outside consultants who file because they act as staff are left out, and so are utilities, banks, universities, other public bodies and retirement income: 76 ties. The payment figure is the largest three-year sum across the years reported.
tables.limits: Disclosure is what the law requires; the question is whether the official took part in decisions that affect the source. Reported income can be a spouse’s salary. Advisory bodies are often built on purpose from people who work in the field, and physicians commonly hold a post at a partner clinic. The forms cannot show whether the person stepped back when the payer’s money was on the table; a recusal notice is required only of members of boards and commissions, so its absence for an employee shows nothing. The source is matched to the payee by name.

sources.t: San Francisco Ethics Commission: Form 700 Schedule A-1 - investments (DataSF)
San Francisco Ethics Commission: Form 700 Schedule A-2 - business entities and trusts (DataSF)
San Francisco Controller: Vendor Payments (Vouchers), totals by payee, department and fiscal year (DataSF)

tables.how: Every investment on Schedule A-1 and every business interest of 10% or more on Schedule A-2 is matched by name to the payees of the filer’s own department, and kept when the department paid the company $50,000 or more in the fiscal years around the report. Shares in large, widely held public companies are left out, and so are outside consultants: 47 ties.
tables.limits: For holding an interest in a City contractor, the question is whether the official takes no part in decisions about it. A manager hired from industry may hold employee-ownership shares from a former employer and be walled off from its contracts. The value is a range the filer ticked, not a share of the company. The company is matched to the payee by name, which can join two firms with one name.

tables.how: The officers, directors and key employees on the latest returns of City-funded nonprofits are compared, by first and last name, with everyone who filed a Form 700 from 2019 on. A pair is kept when the filer’s department paid that nonprofit $100,000 or more and the return falls within a year of the filing years: 93 pairs.
tables.limits: This is a match of names and nothing more: two people can share a name, and no second record ties the officer on the return to the City filer. Where it is one person, the seat is often official (a department head on a partner foundation’s board) or a clinical post at a partner clinic, and it is lawful if the person takes no part in the funding decision.
